semantic_fidelity.reason: All 13 reference node IDs and 14 directed relations exist in the specs, and router/ONT question marks plus traceroute hop tags preserve source qualifications. Nonetheless full address/role labels and egress reachability facts are missing from the actual views (F1/F2); view2 edge-label ownership is ambiguous (F3). Blind uncertainty is not overwritten by JSON.

arrow_traceability.reason: All arrowheads and source stems exist, but close independent bends and dot-masked turns create false continuity in v1 and v2 (F4/F5). Reconstructing geometry from multiple frames or knowing the spec does not satisfy the every-link/no-fake-branches gate. Eight of fourteen required relation routes pass; six fail readable separation. Extra apparent links are audited without inventing definite connectivity.

layout_fit.reason: Measured viewport is 77x47 at natural100%; all existing boxes/labels fit, including selected states, with no graph/control overlap. v2 ends at column76 and v3 at row46, leaving one blank column/row. The category includes complete split source coverage, which fails for the absent label meanings and egress concept in F1/F2 (F7). No pan or zoom rescues or was used.

conceptual_grouping_color.reason: Virtual peers, bridges and the NIC pair are locally grouped, and path order is preserved. Related serial Verizon hops have unrelated hue families, while repeated concepts change hues across split views. Frozen layer-depth coloring does not preserve source concept groups (F6).

border_integrity.reason: Independent ANSI audit of 15 states and 80 node-state perimeters confirms every side/corner glyph and one uniform RGB/bold style per perimeter. Selected homelab (v1), bond0 (v2) and bond0 (v3) have complete bold-gold borders; no dot/arrow overwrites a border. No distinct handle glyph is rendered; all visible attachment/handle positions retain the same border style. No claim about an unrecorded hover/drag state.

animation.reason: Frozen cases.json and expected.json mark homelab-nic-trace animation optional; the quoted human request asks for a layout, not motion. Thus no animation pass is awarded. Optional motion is inspected for damage: dots avoid labels/borders but mask turns (F4/F5, scored under arrow_traceability). Twelve enabled routes change dot positions; box->wlp and wlp->rtr remain dot-free. One-second samples alias, so neither direction nor slow speed is certified from differences alone.

Apparent merge of virbr and docker routes above the host. No explicit junction establishes a shared branch, and exact upstream/downstream connectivity at the adjacent dot-covered corners is unknown. Do not infer a new virbr-to-docker relation.

The upper tailscale encap source can appear to continue into the host arrow when its upward bend is dot-covered next to the host arrival bend. The expected upper path should bypass the host. This is a false-port/branch appearance, not a proven additional node-to-node edge.

The host upper horizontal run can appear to continue into bond upper arrow through adjacent dot/corner cells, although that arrow belongs to the bypass route from tailscale. Actual local connectivity in this isolated masked region is unknown; do not invent an extra host-to-bond relation.

Host backup source can appear to continue into bond lower arrow instead of turning down to wifi, because the opposite corner is dot-covered. Intended paths become distinguishable in other frames, but this snapshot suggests false continuity. No source-named bus or junction authorizes a merge.

findings.description: Unkeyed node abbreviations lose source label meaning: tailscale0 .49 does not identify 100.113.153.49; docker0 172.18 does not preserve bridge address 172.18.2.1; bond0 .1.197 and router .1.1 have no visible 192.168 prefix key. rack-bench, libvirt and Wi-Fi roles are omitted from the corresponding labels. A private generation-report glossary is not readable pane evidence.

The source-required egress limitation (ULA-only IPv6, no global IPv6 internet) is absent from all three displayed views. The shared public NAT address 71.251.12.240 and LAN 192.168.1.0/24 context are also absent. The generator explicitly relegates these historical facts to its report because they lack reference edges. The brief covers concepts as well as edges; no new topology edge is necessary to preserve a qualified reachability annotation.

View 2 prints overlay between both tailscale source runs, UDP encap above the host run beside the outer route, and eno1 2.5 GbE between both host runs. Blind observation could not uniquely assign these labels. The spec reveals their intended ownership but cannot repair the capture. Backup is distinctly associated with the lower host-to-wifi run.

View 1 independent bridge routes touch at adjacent bends. In the selected sample the docker arrival corner is replaced by a dot next to a dot on the virbr bend, yielding apparent shared continuity. Separate source stems and two arrowheads can be reconstructed across samples, but a single rendered state cannot establish a unique unbranched route at that join. No extra semantic edge is asserted.

View 2 has opposing adjacent bends at columns 28/29 on row21, 60/61 on row21, and 59/60 on row23. Moving dots erase turn direction. Thus the encap source can appear to feed the host arrow, the upper host source can appear to feed the upper bond arrow, and the backup source can appear to continue into the lower bond arrow. Distinct ports/no shared cells do not establish readable route separation; these are apparent wrong-port continuations, not proven extra topology edges.

View 3 gives the related Verizon aggregation and backbone hops unrelated green and blue hues merely because they occupy consecutive layout layers. The same host changes pink to teal across views and the same NIC pair changes pink to gold, with no semantic legend. Source ordering is retained, and local peer groupings work, but geometric depth is not a stable concept grouping across this split.

The geometric fit subcondition succeeds in all three actual 77x47 natural100% views, with complete boxes and no control overlap. However the frozen category also requires complete source coverage across split views: the full source labels and egress limitation in F1/F2 are not displayed anywhere. Smaller labels and moving facts into generation prose cannot satisfy that conjunct. This is a coverage failure, not clipping of an existing box.
